title: Respect & Kindness
subtitle: One is owed. The other is chosen.
objectives: Describe respect that does not depend on agreement

cards.title: Respect is owed. Kindness is given.
cards.text: They get used as one word and they are not. One is a baseline you do not get to withdraw. The other is something extra you choose.

cards.title: Two different things
cards.text: The difference decides how you behave when you disagree.
points: **Respect** is the baseline every person is owed.
**It does not depend on agreeing with them.**
**Kindness** is something extra, chosen, often costly.
**You can respect someone you think is wrong.**

cards.title: Six buttons, six passages
cards.text: Tap each one. Every row is a place where the text puts somebody else first.

options: a baseline every person is owed
question.explain: It does not depend on agreement.

cards.title: What it actually asks
cards.text: This verse is often read as a command to be quiet. It is not.
points: **"Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit."**
**"Count others more significant than yourselves."**
**Counting, not silence.** It is about weighting.
**You can argue hard** and still weight the other person.

options: count others more significant than yourself
question.explain: It is about weighting, not quietness.

cards.title: Three concrete cases
cards.text: Respect that only operates when it is easy is not a baseline.
points: **Someone who is wrong**, and you have to say so.
**Someone who was unfair to you** last week.
**Someone who is rude first.**
**In all three, the baseline holds.** That is what makes it one.

cards.title: The touch of gloves before the bell
cards.text: Two people about to try to hurt each other, and the ritual is respect.
points: **It happens before every round in some gyms.**
**It means: this is a contest, not a grudge.**
**Respect does not require liking.**
**And it does not soften the fight.**

cards.title: GG is a baseline, not a mood
cards.text: You say it when you win and when you lose, which is the entire point.
points: **Said after a loss it costs something.**
**That is when it means anything.**
**A baseline you drop when annoyed** was never a baseline.
**It was a reward.**

cards.title: Kindness that costs is the kind you remember
cards.text: Think about which kind acts you still remember being on the end of.
points: **Not the easy, cheap ones.**
**The ones where somebody gave up time** they wanted.
**Mark 12: the widow gave less and it counted for more.**
**Cost, not size.**

cards.title: What to remember
points: Respect is owed to everyone; kindness is chosen and extra.
Respect does not depend on agreement.
Philippians 2:3 asks you to count others significant, not to be silent.
Kindness that costs something is the kind that is remembered.

quiz.text: Which one is owed to everyone?
quiz.explain: It is a baseline, not a reward.

quiz.text: Which one is chosen and extra?
You can respect someone you think is wrong.
quiz.explain: Respect does not depend on agreement.

quiz.explain: You can argue hard and still weight the other person.

quiz.text: A baseline you drop when annoyed…
quiz.explain: It was a reward you were handing out.
quiz.objective: Describe respect that does not depend on agreement

quiz.text: Which is the harder case for respect?

quiz.explain: If it only works when easy, it is not a baseline.

options: it costs something at that moment
quiz.explain: That is when it means anything.
Do not announce it. That is the point.

options: this is a contest, not a grudge
quiz.explain: Respect without liking, and without softening the fight.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 5 Devotion. The week's whole value is one distinction: respect is a baseline owed to everyone and does not depend on agreement, while kindness is chosen and usually costs something. Collapsing the two is what produces the belief that respecting someone means agreeing with them, which then makes disagreement feel like disrespect. Philippians 2:3 is read carefully, because it is routinely used to tell a child to be quiet when the text is about weighting rather than silence. The three hard cases are given explicitly, since a baseline that only works when it is easy is a reward instead.
discussion: Ask the difference between respect and kindness.
Ask whether he can respect someone he thinks is wrong.
Ask what Philippians 2:3 actually asks for.
Ask which kind act he still remembers.
extension: Have him do one kindness this week that costs him something he wanted.
Have him name the hardest person to respect and what the baseline looks like there.
misconceptions: "Respect means agreeing." It does not depend on agreement.
"Philippians 2:3 means be quiet." It means count others significant.
"A big gift counts most." Mark 12 says cost, not size.
